mainTopic: Skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet; letting blood from a בכור and whether one may add a מום to a בעל מום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about skinning a disqualified offering 'from the feet.' The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון might treat a בכור differently, because a בכור's sanctity is weaker than that of other פסולי המוקדשין. It then gives three reasons why skinning from the feet is forbidden even though it might profit הקדש. A new משנה follows, with a ברייתא that expands it, about letting blood from a sick בכור when the cut may cause a מום. The ברייתא gives four views: רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר, the חכמים and רבי שמעון. A teacher tries to match these views to a dispute about a barrel of doubtful-טמא תרומה. The גמרא rejects the match: direct and indirect damage differ, certain death differs from a doubt that אליהו may one day resolve, and the two disputes rest on different פסוקים. Through רבי יוחנן, the גמרא shows that רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue only about adding a מום to an animal that already has one. Each side reads a different half of the פסוק. The amud ends as a ברייתא begins to show that the רבנן learn a ban on causing a מום indirectly (גרמא); the ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not attribute the whole ברייתא to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא did not explain the entire ברייתא according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him establish the entire ברייתא according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא had said that part of the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The גמרא now asks why he did not simply say the whole ברייתא follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is usually better to explain a ברייתא as following one consistent opinion than to split it between different תנאים. If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון fits one part, the גמרא wants to know why he cannot fit all of it. This sets up the next step, which explains why he might not fit the part about a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him establish it / explain it as
All of it, the whole text
A תנא, the son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי

phrases.english: But let him establish the entire [ברייתא]
phrases.notes: The 'him' is רב חסדא, who split the ברייתא earlier.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's earlier decision to split the ברייתא, which came earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's choice to attribute only part of the ברייתא to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single consistent author is preferable, so splitting the ברייתא should not be necessary.

steps.title: A בכור is weaker in sanctity than other disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is only strict with ordinary פסולי המוקדשין, whose sanctity is strong. A בכור is weaker, so he might be lenient there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only said his ruling there, about פסולי המוקדשין, because their sanctity is strong enough to pass onto their redemption money. But a בכור, whose sanctity is not strong enough to pass onto its redemption money, is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view may apply only to regular disqualified offerings, not to a בכור. So the part of the ברייתא about a בכור could follow a different view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular פסולי המוקדשין are redeemed, and their holiness passes onto the redemption money. That shows their sanctity is strong. A בכור has no such redemption, so its sanctity is considered weaker. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון might therefore treat a slaughtered blemished בכור more leniently and allow it to be skinned from the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
He only said his ruling up to here, meaning in this case alone
Consecrated animals that became disqualified, usually through a blemish
They are strong
To transfer its sanctity onto its redemption money
A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that 'consecrated' is not one uniform level. A בכור is still holy, but its sanctity has its own unique, weaker profile when it comes to redemption.

Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, there

phrases.english: but a firstborn,

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (ordinary פסולי המוקדשין versus בכור)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strictness applies to every consecrated animal, including a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: His strictness may apply only to offerings whose sanctity is strong enough to pass onto redemption money, which excludes a בכור.

steps.title: Why forbid skinning from the feet if it benefits הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון surely accepts the משנה permitting market sales by weight because that benefits הקדש. Skinning from the feet should then be allowed for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון not hold the rule that all פסולי המוקדשין are sold in the butchers' market and weighed by the litra? Evidently, since there is profit for הקדש, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view. If the משנה allows money-making practices because they help הקדש, skinning from the feet should be allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets disqualified offerings be sold like ordinary meat, in the market and by weight, even though they keep some holiness. The reason is that this raises their value. A buyer then pays more to redeem the animal, and הקדש gains. Skinning from the feet also raises value, because the whole hide sells for more, so the same logic should permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it
The butchers' market
A litra, a unit of weight
Evidently, this shows that
Profit for the Temple treasury

steps.confusionAlert: The 'benefit to הקדש' is indirect. הקדש itself does not sell the meat. The point is that if the meat can be sold profitably later, people will pay more to redeem the animal in the first place.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, not hold of
[the rule that] all disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the butchers' market
and weighed by the litra?
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה on 31a.

phrases.english: Evidently, since there is profit for the Temple treasury,
he permits it!
phrases.notes: So skinning from the feet should be permitted too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having accepted that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is strict for פסולי המוקדשין, the גמרא now questions the basis for that strictness.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's ban on skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's principle that profit for הקדש justifies treating the meat like ordinary meat should also permit skinning from the feet.

steps.title: No real profit: the gain to the hide damages the meat
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא answers that skinning from the feet gives no net gain, because it damages the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא said: what improves the hide damages the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question by saying there is no real profit for הקדש here. Whatever is gained on the hide is lost on the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning from the feet keeps the hide whole, but some flesh gets cut off along with it. The meat's value drops by about as much as the hide's value rises. With no net gain for הקדש, the reason that permitted market sales does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Improves, increases the value
Hide, skin
Damages, reduces the value

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
what improves the hide damages the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise (there is no real profit)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skinning from the feet brings profit to הקדש, just like market sales do.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gain to the hide is cancelled out by the loss to the meat, so there is no profit to justify it.

steps.title: It looks like working with קדשים
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they say in the name of רבינא that skinning from the feet is forbidden because it looks like working with consecrated animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West, in the name of רבינא, they say: because it looks like performing work with קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer, from the scholars of ארץ ישראל. Even if there is profit, skinning from the feet is forbidden because of how it looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that there may be profit, but adds a different problem. Skinning from the feet involves extra handling that resembles doing work with holy animals, which is forbidden. Even after the animal is redeemed and slaughtered, the appearance itself is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Looks like, appears as
Doing work with consecrated animals, which is forbidden

phrases.english: In the West they say in the name of Ravina:
because it appears as though he is performing work with consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to step 3, alongside רב מרי's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Profit for הקדש should be enough to permit skinning from the feet.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is still forbidden because it looks like doing work with קדשים.

steps.title: A decree so he will not raise herds from them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין says the ban is a rabbinic decree, out of concern that the owner will raise whole herds from these animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין says: it is a decree, lest he raise many herds from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer: the prohibition is a rabbinic גזירה meant to stop the owner from keeping these animals alive and breeding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If skinning whole hides were profitable, the owner might hold onto the animals while waiting for a hide buyer. Meanwhile they would multiply into herds, and he might come to shear or work them, which is forbidden. To block that path, the Rabbis banned skinning from the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree, a protective fence
Lest, out of concern that
Herds, flocks

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge was that profit for הקדש should permit skinning from the feet. There are three answers. 1) רב מרי: there is no real profit, because the meat is damaged. 2) רבינא, in the West: it looks like working with קדשים. 3) רבי יוסי בר אבין: a גזירה, lest he keep and breed the animals into herds.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin says:
[It is] a decree, lest he raise from them
many herds.
phrases.notes: Doubling the word means 'herd after herd,' many herds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 3, offering a different reason from the first two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there is profit, skinning from the feet should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Rabbis forbade it as a safeguard, so the owner would not keep the animals and come to raise herds from them.

steps.title: The משנה: May we let blood from a sick firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records three opinions about bloodletting a בכור that is congested with blood. רבי יהודה says never. The חכמים say yes, but without making a מום. רבי שמעון says yes, even if a מום is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn animal that is overcome by too much blood: even if it will die, we do not let its blood. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: he may let its blood, as long as he does not make a blemish in it. If he did make a blemish, he may not slaughter the animal because of that blemish. רבי שמעון says: he may let its blood even though he makes a blemish in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It asks whether we may let blood from a sick בכור when the cut might cause a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש once it has a מום, so causing a מום on purpose is forbidden. רבי יהודה protects that rule even at the cost of the animal's life. The חכמים allow saving the animal but do not let the owner benefit from a מום he caused. רבי שמעון allows the bloodletting even if a מום results.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
That is seized or congested with too much blood
Letting blood, meaning cutting a vein to release blood
A permanent blemish that allows a בכור to be slaughtered
He may not slaughter the animal on account of that blemish

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a מום is something bad for the owner. For a בכור, a מום is actually what allows the owner to slaughter and eat it. That is exactly why making one on purpose is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: no bloodletting, even if the animal will die. חכמים: bloodletting is allowed without making a מום, and an animal blemished this way may not be slaughtered on that מום. רבי שמעון: bloodletting is allowed even if it makes a מום.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Four opinions on bloodletting a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four views: רבי מאיר, the חכמים, רבי שמעון, and רבי יהודה. It makes clear exactly where each one stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A firstborn congested with blood may have its blood let in a place where the cut does not make a blemish. It may not have its blood let in a place where the cut makes a blemish. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: even in a place where it makes a blemish, as long as he does not slaughter the animal because of that blemish. רבי שמעון says: it may even be slaughtered because of that blemish. רבי יהודה says: even if it will die, we do not let its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that spells out the same dispute in more detail, with four opinions instead of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a ladder from strict to lenient. רבי יהודה allows no bloodletting at all. רבי מאיר allows it only in a spot that will not cause a מום. The חכמים allow even a spot that causes a מום, but not slaughter because of it. רבי שמעון allows slaughter even because of that מום. Note that the view called 'חכמים' in the משנה matches רבי מאיר's view here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught, which introduces a ברייתא
In a spot where cutting does not cause a blemish
On the basis of that same blemish

steps.confusionAlert: The name 'חכמים' does not refer to the same opinion in the משנה and the ברייתא. The משנה's חכמים (no מום allowed) match רבי מאיר in the ברייתא. The ברייתא's חכמים (a מום is allowed, but no slaughter on it) are a separate, more lenient view.
steps.whatToRemember: Four levels, from strict to lenient: רבי יהודה (never), רבי מאיר (only where no מום results), חכמים (even with a מום, but no slaughter on it), רבי שמעון (even slaughter on that מום).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's three-way dispute into a fuller four-way dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: bloodletting only where no מום results. חכמים: even where a מום results, but no slaughter on it. רבי שמעון: even slaughter on it. רבי יהודה: no bloodletting even to save the animal's life.

steps.title: The same dispute appears with a barrel of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (some say רבי חייא) taught his son that the bloodletting dispute is matched by a dispute about a barrel of תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר taught his son, and some say it was רבי חייא who taught his son: Just as there is a dispute here, so there is a dispute about a barrel of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A teacher links our dispute to another dispute about תרומה. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes that other משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that the two cases share the same basic argument. The question is how far we must protect something holy when it may already be compromised or at risk. The details of the parallel come from the quoted source in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the dispute in the ברייתא to a dispute in another area of halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bloodletting dispute parallels the dispute about a barrel of תרומה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the תרומה barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in תרומות. רבי אליעזר says that even a barrel of תרומה with a ספק טומאה must still be protected: move it to a hidden place, and cover it if it is open.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A barrel of תרומה that developed a doubt about whether it became טמא. רבי אליעזר says: if it was in an exposed place, he should put it in a hidden place. If it was uncovered, he should cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source text it just mentioned. This is the first part of the תרומה משנה, which gives רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though this תרומה is doubtful and cannot be eaten, רבי אליעזר says we must still actively guard it from becoming definitely טמא. That strict protective attitude is the side of the parallel that matches the stricter views about the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A doubt about whether something became ritually impure
A vulnerable, exposed place where impurity might reach it
A hidden, protected place
Uncovered

steps.title: The rest of the barrel משנה: רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in תרומות. רבי יהושע says one may move the barrel to an exposed place and uncover it. רבן גמליאל says to change nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: if the barrel was in a hidden place, he may put it in an exposed place. If it was covered, he may uncover it. רבן גמליאל says: he should not do anything new with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it started in step 10, so that we now have all three opinions about the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said to keep guarding the doubtful תרומה. רבי יהושע goes to the other extreme: you may even put it where it will become טמא. רבן גמליאל takes the middle road: don't guard it more and don't expose it more, just leave it as it is.

steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות, the opinions of רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל

steps.title: Matching each bloodletting opinion to a barrel opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lines up the opinions: רבי מאיר matches רבי אליעזר, the רבנן match רבי יהושע, and רבי יהודה matches רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds like רבי אליעזר. The רבנן hold like רבי יהושע. רבי יהודה holds like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly how the two arguments line up, one opinion against the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows bloodletting only without causing a מום. That is like רבי אליעזר, who says don't let the holy item become damaged. The רבנן allow it even with a מום, like רבי יהושע, who lets the barrel become טמא. רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting entirely, like רבן גמליאל, who says to do nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Like; holds the same view as
The Sages (here, those in the ברייתא who allow bloodletting even with a מום)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names. In the ברייתא (step 8), רבי מאיר is the one who says 'yes, but without a מום,' and the רבנן are the ones who say 'even with a מום.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir is like Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: Allow bloodletting but don't cause a מום = keep guarding the barrel.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis are like Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: Even with a מום = you may even expose the barrel.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda is like Rabban Gamliel.
phrases.notes: Don't bloodlet at all = don't do anything new.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְרַבָּנַן כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the full barrel משנה to state the exact parallel promised in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three bloodletting opinions match the three barrel opinions: רבי מאיר = רבי אליעזר, רבנן = רבי יהושע, רבי יהודה = רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי מאיר might not match רבי אליעזר: direct versus indirect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know. Maybe רבי מאיר is strict only with the בכור, where a person makes the מום with his own hands. With the barrel, the impurity comes only indirectly, so he might agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe רבי מאיר only said his view there, by the בכור, because the person makes the damage with his own hands. But here, by the barrel, where he only indirectly causes it, he might hold like רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the matching from step 12 and starts breaking it apart, beginning with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a מום into a בכור is a direct act of damage. Leaving a barrel exposed so that it might become טמא later is only indirect causing (גרמא). So רבי מאיר could be strict about the first and lenient about the second, and the match fails.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? (opens a challenge)
He only said his view up to this point, meaning only in that case
With his own hands; direct action
Indirect causing

phrases.english: From where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Meir only said his view there,
phrases.notes: There = the בכור.

phrases.english: because he is acting with his own hands;
but here, where it is only indirect causing,
phrases.notes: Here = the barrel.

phrases.english: he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the parallel just stated in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match of רבי מאיר to רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases differ: the בכור involves direct damage (בידים), while the barrel involves only indirect causing (גרמא).

steps.title: רבי אליעזר might not match רבי מאיר: a far-off hope versus sure death
steps.stepSummary: Likewise, maybe רבי אליעזר guards the barrel only because אליהו might someday come and declare it טהור. By the בכור, the animal will surely die if left alone, so he might agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי אליעזר only said his view there, by the barrel, because perhaps אליהו will come and declare it טהור. But here, by the בכור, where if he leaves it the animal will die, he might hold like the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the same match from the other side, showing that רבי אליעזר might also not hold like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר protects the barrel because there is still hope it may turn out to be טהור. By the בכור the danger is certain, since the animal will die without bloodletting. So he might allow bloodletting even with a מום, like the רבנן. Now the claimed parallel looks shaky in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו the prophet, who in the future will settle open doubts
And will declare it pure
Leaves alone
Dies

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא first matched the two arguments one opinion to another. Then it showed that each case has its own reasons: direct versus indirect damage, and a far-off hope versus certain loss. Because of this, a person could hold one way in one case and differently in the other.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer only said his view there,
phrases.notes: There = the barrel of תרומה.

phrases.english: because perhaps Eliyahu will come and declare it pure;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית —
phrases.english: but here, where if he leaves it alone it will die,
phrases.notes: Here = the בכור.

phrases.english: he holds like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּא יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וִיטַהֲרֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rejection begun in step 13, now from רבי אליעזר's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match of רבי אליעזר to רבי מאיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The barrel still has hope of being טהור through אליהו, while the בכור faces certain death, so the reasons for being strict do not carry over.

steps.title: The רבנן might agree with רבי אליעזר about the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן allow letting blood by the בכור only because the animal will surely die. By the barrel, they might agree with רבי אליעזר and guard it, since אליהו might come and declare it טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe the רבנן only said their view here, by the בכור, because if you leave the animal alone it will die. But there, by the barrel, where אליהו might come and declare it טהור, they could hold like רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps breaking apart the match from Step 12. Now it shows that the רבנן do not have to agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 matched the lenient רבנן of the בכור with lenient רבי יהושע of the barrel. Here the גמרא shows the רבנן might be lenient only because the בכור faces certain death. The barrel faces no such danger, and it might still turn out to be טהור. So the רבנן could be strict there, like רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said their view up to here (in this case alone)
Leaves alone, lets be
It dies
אליהו the prophet, who will settle doubts in the future
They hold, they are of the opinion

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis only said their view here (by the firstborn),
because if one leaves it alone, it will die;
phrases.notes: Certain loss of the animal is the reason for leniency.

phrases.english: but there (by the barrel of terumah),
where perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure,
they could hold like Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as Step 14, but turned around, to break the second pair.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match between the רבנן (בכור) and רבי יהושע (barrel).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן's leniency may depend on the certain death of the בכור, which the barrel case lacks.

steps.title: רבי יהודה might agree with רבי יהושע about the barrel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids letting blood only because a person would make the מום with his own hands. With the barrel, the טומאה comes only indirectly, so he might be lenient like רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי יהודה only said his view here, by the בכור, because the person acts with his own hands. But there, by the barrel, where the harm is only indirect, he could hold like רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the third pair from Step 12. It shows that רבי יהודה does not have to agree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is the strictest about the בכור: no letting blood at all. This step uses the same reasoning as Step 13. Making a מום directly with your hands is worse than causing טומאה indirectly. So רבי יהודה could be strict by the בכור and still be lenient by the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: With one's own hands, by direct action
Indirect causation
Does, acts

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda only said his view here (by the firstborn),
because the person is acting with his own hands;
but there, where it is only indirect,
he could hold like Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the direct-versus-indirect reasoning of Step 13 to break the third pair.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match between רבי יהודה (בכור) and רבן גמליאל (barrel).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's strictness may come from the direct action by the בכור, which is missing by the barrel.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל might agree with the רבנן about the בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says to leave the barrel alone only because אליהו might declare it טהור. By the בכור, which will surely die, he might agree with the רבנן and allow letting blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבן גמליאל only said his view there, by the barrel, because אליהו might come and declare it טהור. But here, by the בכור, where if you leave it alone it will die, he could hold like the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the same third pair from the other side. Now it shows that רבן גמליאל does not have to agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that רבי יהודה might not match רבן גמליאל. This step shows that רבן גמליאל might not match רבי יהודה either. His 'change nothing' ruling may depend on the hope that the barrel will turn out טהור. By the בכור there is certain death, so he could be lenient. Now every pairing from Step 12 has been taken apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will declare it pure

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא might be strict in one case and lenient in the other. Two reasons explain why. First, direct action (by the בכור) is worse than indirect harm (by the barrel). Second, certain death (by the בכור) is different from a doubt that might be resolved (by the barrel). So the two disputes cannot be lined up.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabban Gamliel only said his view there (by the barrel),
because perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית,
phrases.english: but here, where if one leaves it alone it will die,
he could hold like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of every pairing proposed in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match between רבן גמליאל (barrel) and רבי יהודה (בכור).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבן גמליאל's ruling may rest on the hope of the barrel's טהרה, which does not apply to the dying בכור.

steps.title: A second rejection: each dispute is based on different verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another reason the disputes cannot be compared: each one depends on how the תנאים read different פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: here they argue about verses, and there they argue about verses (different ones).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate rejection of the comparison. This line sets up the source that comes next to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the rejections were based on reasoning about each case. Now the גמרא says the בכור dispute comes from how the תנאים read certain פסוקים, and the barrel dispute from others. Since the disputes have different roots, a person's view in one tells us nothing about his view in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces an additional argument)
They disagree about verses

phrases.english: And furthermore,
here they disagree about verses,
and there they disagree about (other) verses,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָכָא בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new kind of rejection, based on the source of each dispute instead of the details of each case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two disputes come from different פסוקים, so they are independent of each other.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: leavening a מנחה that is already leavened is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that everyone agrees a person who leavens a מנחה after someone else already leavened it is liable. This comes from two פסוקים: 'לא תאפה חמץ' and 'לא תעשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that one who leavens a מנחה after another person already leavened it is liable. This is because it is written 'it shall not be baked חמץ' and also 'it shall not be made' with חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing a source to explain the verse-based argument of Step 18. It opens with a case where everyone agrees: doing a forbidden act again, after it was already done, is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate פסוקים about making a מנחה חמץ. One is used for the first act of leavening. The extra one teaches liability even for leavening it again afterward. This sets up the bigger question of damaging something that is already damaged, which relates to making a מום on the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
One who leavens after another already leavened
Liable (to punishment)
'It shall not be baked leavened' (ויקרא ו:י)
'It shall not be made' leavened (ויקרא ב:יא)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
All agree regarding one who leavens after one who leavened
that he is liable,
as it is written: 'It shall not be baked leavened'
and 'It shall not be made' (leavened).
phrases.notes: Two verses: one for the first leavening, one for leavening again.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that backs up Step 18's claim that the disputes depend on פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leavening a מנחה that someone already leavened still makes one liable, learned from the double phrasing in the פסוקים.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: castrating an already-castrated animal is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Everyone also agrees that one who castrates an animal after someone else already castrated it is liable. The פסוק already forbids 'cut', so it did not need to list 'detached', which is the worse injury. The extra word 'detached' teaches that detaching after cutting is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone agrees about one who castrates after another already castrated, that he is liable. As it is written: 'bruised, crushed, detached, or cut.' If one is liable for cutting, is he not surely liable for detaching? Rather, the פסוק comes to include one who detaches after another cut, that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי יוחנן's teaching with a second example: castrating an animal that was already castrated is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Detaching is a worse injury than cutting. So the פסוק did not need to list detaching to forbid it. The extra word teaches a new case: someone who detaches after the cutting was already done is liable. This shows the Torah forbids further damage even to an animal that is already damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: One who castrates after another already castrated
Detaching (the more severe injury)
Cutting (the lesser injury)
Is it not all the more so?
To include (a new case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the רבותא. Both examples (חמץ and סירוס) are cases where EVERYONE agrees. The גמרא brings them to set up a contrast with a case where the תנאים DO argue about the פסוקים. That case is the בכור.

phrases.english: (All agree) regarding one who castrates after one who castrated
that he is liable,
as it is written: 'Bruised or crushed
or detached or cut,'
if one is liable for cutting,
then for detaching, all the more so!
Rather, it comes to include one who detaches after one who cut,
that he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְסָרֵס אַחַר מְסָרֵס שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example in the same רבי יוחנן statement, parallel to מחמץ אחר מחמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Castrating an animal that was already castrated still makes one liable, learned from the extra word in the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next idea: whether one may make a מום on an animal that already has a מום. That is the verse-based root of the בכור dispute.

steps.title: The only real dispute: adding a blemish to an already blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement between רבי מאיר and the רבנן is limited to one case: מטיל מום בבעל מום. רבי מאיר forbids it because of 'כל מום לא יהיה בו'. The רבנן permit it because of 'תמים יהיה לרצון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about someone who makes a blemish in an animal that already has a blemish. רבי מאיר holds: 'No blemish at all shall be in it.' The רבנן hold: 'It shall be perfect to be accepted.'
steps.whatsHappening: After listing the cases where everyone agrees, the גמרא now names the one case where רבי מאיר and the רבנן actually argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'כל מום', meaning any blemish, so even a second blemish on an already blemished animal is forbidden. The רבנן read 'תמים יהיה לרצון' as saying the ban protects only an animal that is still perfect and fit for the מזבח. Once it already has a מום, there is nothing left to protect.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who causes a blemish in an animal
An animal that already has a blemish
'There shall be no blemish at all in it' (ויקרא כב:כא)
'It shall be perfect to be accepted' (same פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases come from the same פסוק. Each side builds its view on a different half of that one verse.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact boundary of the dispute. Adding damage after damage is agreed to be forbidden by מנחה and castration, but by מומים it is debated.

phrases.english: They did not disagree except
about one who causes a blemish in an already blemished animal,
for Rabbi Meir holds:
'There shall be no blemish at all in it,'
phrases.notes: 'Any' blemish includes a second one.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
'It shall be perfect to be accepted.'
phrases.notes: The ban applies only while the animal is still perfect.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּמֵטִיל מוּם בְּבַעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's list. After the agreed cases, it names the single disputed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids adding a מום to a בעל מום (כל מום). The רבנן permit it (תמים יהיה לרצון).

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר use the other half of the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from 'תמים יהיה לרצון', since he does not use it the way the רבנן do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with this phrase, 'It shall be perfect to be accepted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question: every phrase in the תורה must teach something, so what does רבי מאיר learn from the רבנן's phrase? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not read 'תמים' as limiting the ban to perfect animals. That leaves the phrase looking unused in his view. The גמרא wants to find what it teaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does he do with it?' A question asking how a Tanna uses a verse

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
this phrase 'It shall be perfect to be accepted'
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי מאיר uses the verse the רבנן relied on in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from 'תמים יהיה לרצון'.

steps.title: First answer: it excludes an animal born blemished
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that, for רבי מאיר, 'תמים' excludes an animal that had a מום from birth. Adding a blemish to such an animal would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to exclude an animal that was blemished from the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer: רבי מאיר uses 'תמים' to permit adding a blemish only to an animal born with one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would make רבי מאיר's ban cover any animal that was once perfect, even if it later got a מום. Only an animal born blemished would be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it' for a different teaching
From the very start, from birth

phrases.english: He needs it
to exclude an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תמים' excludes an animal born with a מום.

steps.title: That is obvious: it is just like a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that an animal born blemished obviously has no ban on blemishing. It never had real קדושת הגוף, so a verse is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal blemished from the outset? That is obvious. It is just like a palm tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first answer. No פסוק is needed to teach something this obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born with a מום could never be offered. Its holiness is only monetary, like a consecrated palm tree, which no one would think has a ban on 'blemishing'. So 'תמים' cannot be teaching this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious.' The verse would be teaching nothing new
Merely a palm tree, meaning it has only monetary holiness and no קדושת הגוף

phrases.english: An animal blemished from the outset? That is obvious,
it is merely a palm tree!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ — פְּשִׁיטָא, דִּיקְלָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תמים' excludes an animal born blemished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal with no קדושת הגוף obviously has no ban on blemishing, so a verse would be wasted on it.

steps.title: Final answer: it excludes redeemed disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: Instead, רבי מאיר uses 'תמים' to exclude פסולי המוקדשין after פדיון. Since they stay forbidden in shearing and work, one might think blemishing them is also forbidden. The verse teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude disqualified consecrated animals after they are redeemed. You might have thought: since they are still forbidden to be sheared or worked, they should also be forbidden to be blemished. The verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for what 'תמים' teaches רבי מאיר. It teaches a case that is not obvious at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeemed פסולי המוקדשין keep some holiness: you still may not shear them or work them. That makes it reasonable to think blemishing them is also forbidden. The verse is needed to say the ban on מומים does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became disqualified because of a blemish
Their redemption, which makes them non-sacred for eating
Shearing and working the animal, which stay forbidden even after redemption
'You might have thought.' Explains why the verse is needed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: 'כל מום' forbids adding a מום even to a בעל מום. 'תמים יהיה לרצון' only frees redeemed פסולי המוקדשין from the ban. רבנן: 'תמים' means the ban protects only a perfect animal.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude
disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption,
for it might enter your mind to say:
since they are forbidden in shearing and labor,
let them also be forbidden regarding blemishes,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַעוֹטֵי פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 23 after the objection in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a different, non-obvious case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since redeemed פסולי המוקדשין are still forbidden in shearing and work, blemishing them should also be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תמים יהיה לרצון' teaches that there is no ban on blemishing redeemed פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'There shall not be any blemish in it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. The רבנן also have the verse 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' in front of them, so what do they learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too: isn't it written, 'There shall not be any blemish in it'? What do they learn from that verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Before, the גמרא asked what רבי מאיר does with the רבנן's verse. Now it asks the same question in reverse: what do the רבנן do with רבי מאיר's verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר used 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' to forbid adding a blemish to an animal that is already blemished. The רבנן do not learn that from it. Since every verse must teach something, the רבנן must use this verse for some other lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי מאיר
Also / too
But isn't it written...?
'There shall not be any blemish in it' (ויקרא כב:כא)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
phrases.notes: This mirrors the question about רבי מאיר in step 22.

phrases.english: isn't it written: 'There shall not be any blemish in it'!
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's source verse. What do the רבנן do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 22. Having explained רבי מאיר's use of the רבנן's verse, the גמרא now asks how the רבנן use רבי מאיר's verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson do the רבנן draw from 'כל מום לא יהיה בו', since they do not use it to forbid מטיל מום בבעל מום?

steps.title: The verse comes to forbid causing a blemish indirectly
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' to teach that even causing a blemish indirectly (גרמא) is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to teach about an indirect cause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, for the רבנן, this verse teaches the ban on causing a blemish indirectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A direct blemish means you cut the animal yourself. An indirect blemish (גרמא) means you set things up so the blemish happens on its own, without your hand doing it. According to the רבנן, this verse expands the ban to include the indirect case too.

keyTerms.meaning: An indirect cause. You set up a situation that leads to the result, but do not do the act yourself.
It comes for... (this verse is needed to teach...)

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer shows that both sides use both verses. They only differ in what each verse teaches. This is a common pattern in the גמרא.

phrases.english: It comes for an indirect cause,
phrases.notes: Causing a blemish indirectly is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִגְרָמָא הוּא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn from 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' that causing a blemish indirectly (גרמא) is also forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins to show the indirect-blemish teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that learns the גרמא ban from this verse. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'There shall not be any blemish in it' — from this I only know...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its answer with a ברייתא. This is a setup line: the ברייתא has just started, and its point comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אין לי' ('I only have') signal a familiar pattern. First the verse gives a basic case (a direct blemish). Then another word in the verse adds a further case (an indirect blemish). This seems to be built on the extra word 'כל', so look for that move in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
I only have... (the verse at first teaches only this basic case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at 'אין לי'. It is not the conclusion. It starts a two-part pattern: 'I only have X... how do I know Y?' The real point comes next.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'There shall not be a blemish in it'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא quotes the verse.

phrases.english: — I have only...
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״מוּם לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ״ — אֵין לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support step 27's claim that the verse teaches the גרמא ban.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the רבנן learn the ban on indirect blemishing from 'כל מום לא יהיה בו'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explains the verse 'מום לא יהיה בו' (quote cut off at 'אין לי').
